Verdict: refuse. Don't buy this one.

Key reasons from the brief:
- Operator signal is absent. Bundle share is 36%, and the first two minutes show a launch bot and a 0.77 sell-to-buy ratio, so this isn't the operator-backed profile that has been roughly break-even.
- Flow is negative. The last 15 minutes show net outflow of -0.48 SOL, sell volume matching buy volume, and a -3% return, with a 23% drawdown from the 30-minute high.
- Pool depth is thin at 89.5 SOL, so a $20 round trip with 1.4-5.1% costs plus impact is unfavorable.
- The name and symbol mirror a known meme ticker. Treat that as a weak signal of copycat or confusion trading, not as information.

If the desk overrides, the most I'd accept is $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. I'd still expect a loss.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying wifween now is weak. Buying pressure is real in raw terms: 126 buyers and 39.9 SOL bought over the last 15 minutes, and the first two minutes after graduation drew 86 buyers. The curve isn't dominated by a few wallets (top3 share 21.6%, top5 at the start 27.2%).

But the flow is flat. Net flow over 15 minutes is -0.48 SOL, sells nearly matched buys (40.4 vs 39.9), the coin is 23.5% off its 30-minute high and down 11.9% over 30 minutes, and early sell-to-buy pressure was 0.77. Nothing here shows demand accelerating or holding, and the 36% bundle share plus a launch bot suggests some of the early buying was engineered rather than organic. Against a ~20% base-rate loss and ~3-5% round-trip costs, I don't see a case that clears the bar. Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: a rug or insider distribution, with fees eating whatever small bounce remains.

The strongest signal is the bundle: 36.3% of the curve was bought through bundles, and the completer holds 1.63x its own share, which points to coordinated buying rather than organic demand. The 30-minute high has already fallen 23.5%, and the coin is down 11.9% since launch. Over the last 15 minutes, sells (40.37 SOL) matched buys (39.89 SOL), so net flow is -0.48 SOL, with 99 sellers against 126 buyers. Early exits look heavy: a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.774 in the first two minutes after graduation, with a launch bot present.

Dead volume is a risk too. With a $20 ticket and a 1.4-5.1% round trip on an 89.5 SOL pool, a modest move can be fully absorbed by costs.

Skip.
